The effect of the judgment on the righteous, as contrasted with its effect on the wicked (Mal 4:1). To the wicked it shall be as an oven that consumes the stubble (<reference osisRef="Matt.6.30">Mt 6:30</reference>); to the righteous it shall be the advent of the gladdening Sun, not of condemnation, but "of righteousness"; not destroying, but "healing" (<reference osisRef="Jer.23.6">Jr 23:6</reference>).<div eID="gen25095" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25096" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">you that fear my name--</hi>The same as those in Mal 3:16, who confessed God amidst abounding blasphemy (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.5">Is 66:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.10.32">Mt 10:32</reference>). The spiritual blessings brought by Him are summed up in the two, "righteousness" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.1.30">1Co 1:30</reference>) and spiritual "healing" (<reference osisRef="Ps.103.3">Psa 103:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.57.19">Is 57:19</reference>). Those who walk in the dark now may take comfort in the certainty that they shall walk hereafter in eternal light (<reference osisRef="Isa.50.10">Is 50:10</reference>).<div eID="gen25096" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25097" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in his wings--</hi>implying the winged swiftness with which He shall appear (compare "suddenly," Mal 3:1) for the relief of His people. The beams of the Sun are His "wings." Compare "wings of the morning," <reference osisRef="Ps.139.9">Psa 139:9</reference>. The "Sun" gladdening the righteous is suggested by the previous "day" of terror consuming the wicked. Compare as to Christ, <reference osisRef="2Sam.23.4">2Sa 23:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.84.11">Psa 84:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.1.78">Lu 1:78</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.9">Joh 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.8.12">8:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.5.14">Ep 5:14</reference>; and in His second coming, <reference osisRef="2Pet.1.19">2Pe 1:19</reference>. The Church is the moon reflecting His light (<reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Re 12:1</reference>). The righteous shall by His righteousness "shine as the Sun in the kingdom of the Father" (<reference osisRef="Matt.13.43">Mt 13:43</reference>).<div eID="gen25097" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25098" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye shall go forth--</hi>from the straits in which you were, as it were, held captive. An earnest of this was given in the escape of the Christians to Pella before the destruction of Jerusalem.<div eID="gen25098" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25099" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">grow up--</hi>rather, "leap" as frisking calves [Calvin]; literally, "spread," "take a wide range."<div eID="gen25099" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25100" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as calves of the stall--</hi>which when set free from the stall disport with joy (<reference osisRef="Acts.8.8">Ac 8:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.13.52">13:52</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.20.24">20:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.14.17">Ro 14:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.5.22">Ga 5:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.1.4">Php 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.1.8">1Pe 1:8</reference>). Especially the godly shall rejoice at their final deliverance at Christ's second coming (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.10">Is 61:10</reference>). <div eID="gen25100" type="x-p"/>

Yea, the righteous shall be the army attending Christ in His final destruction of the ungodly (<reference osisRef="2Sam.22.43">2Sa 22:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.49.14">Psa 49:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.47.3">47:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.7.10">Mi 7:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.10.5">Zec 10:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.6.2">1Co 6:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.26">Re 2:26</reference>, 27; 19:14, 15).<div eID="gen25101" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25102" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ashes--</hi>after having been burnt with the fire of judgment (Mal 4:1). <div eID="gen25102" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13266"/><div sID="gen25103" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13266"/><hi type="bold">4. Remember ... law--</hi>"The law and all the prophets" were to be in force until John (<reference osisRef="Matt.11.13">Mt 11:13</reference>), no prophet intervening after Malachi; therefore they are told, "Remember the law," for in the absence of living prophets, they were likely to forget it. The office of Christ's forerunner was to bring them back to the law, which they had too much forgotten, and so "to make ready a people prepared for the Lord" at His coming (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.17">Lu 1:17</reference>). God withheld prophets for a time that men might seek after Christ with the greater desire [Calvin]. The history of human advancement is marked by periods of rest, and again progress. So in Revelation: it is given for a time; then during its suspension men live on the memories of the past. After Malachi there was a silence of four hundred years; then a harbinger of light in the wilderness, ushering in the brightest of all the lights that had been manifested, but short-lived; then eighteen centuries during which we have been guided by the light which shone in that last manifestation. The silence has been longer than before, and will be succeeded by a more glorious and awful revelation than ever. John the Baptist was to "restore" the defaced image of "the law," so that the original might be recognized when it appeared among men [Hinds]. Just as "Moses" and "Elias" are here connected with the Lord's coming, so at the transfiguration they converse with Him, implying that the law and prophets which had prepared His way were now fulfilled in Him.<div eID="gen25103" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25104" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">statutes ... judgments--</hi>ceremonial "statutes": "judgments" in civil questions at issue. "The law" refers to morals and religion. <div eID="gen25104" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13267"/><div sID="gen25105" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13267"/><hi type="bold">5. I send you Elijah--</hi>as a means towards your "remembering the law" (Mal 4:4).<div eID="gen25105" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25106" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the prophet--</hi>emphatical; not "the Tishbite"; for it is in his official, not his personal capacity, that his coming is here predicted. In this sense, John the Baptist was an Elijah in spirit (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.16">Lu 1:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.17">17</reference>), but not the literal Elijah; whence when asked, "Art thou Elias?" (<reference osisRef="John.1.21">Joh 1:21</reference>), He answered, "I am not." "Art thou that prophet?" "No." This implies that John, though knowing from the angel's announcement to his father that he was referred to by Mal 4:5 (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.17">Lu 1:17</reference>), whence he wore the costume of Elijah, yet knew by inspiration that he did not exhaustively fulfil all that is included in this prophecy: that there is a further fulfilment (compare Note, see on Mal 3:1). As Moses in Mal 4:4 represents the law, so Elijah represents the prophets. The Jews always understood it of the literal Elijah. Their saying is, "Messiah must be anointed by Elijah." As there is another consummating advent of Messiah Himself, so also of His forerunner Elijah; perhaps in person, as at the transfiguration (<reference osisRef="Matt.17.3">Mt 17:3</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Matt.17.11">Mt 17:11</reference>). He in his appearance at the transfiguration in that body on which death had never passed is the forerunner of the saints who shall be found alive at the Lord's second coming. <reference osisRef="Rev.11.3">Re 11:3</reference> may refer to the same witnesses as at the transfiguration, Moses and Elijah; <reference osisRef="Rev.11.6">Re 11:6</reference> identifies the latter (compare <reference osisRef="1Kgs.17.1">1Ki 17:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jas.5.17">Jas 5:17</reference>). Even after the transfiguration Jesus (<reference osisRef="Matt.17.11">Mt 17:11</reference>) speaks of Elijah's coming "to restore all things" as still future, though He adds that Elijah (in the person of John the Baptist) is come already in a sense (compare <reference osisRef="Acts.3.21">Ac 3:21</reference>). However, the future forerunner of Messiah at His second coming may be a prophet or number of prophets clothed with Elijah's power, who, with zealous upholders of "the law" clothed in the spirit of "Moses," may be the forerunning witnesses alluded to here and in <reference osisRef="Rev.11.2-Rev.11.12">Re 11:2-12</reference>. The words "before the ... dreadful day of the Lord," show that John cannot be exclusively meant; for he came before the day of Christ's coming in grace, not before His coming in terror, of which last the destruction of Jerusalem was the earnest (Mal 4:1; <reference osisRef="Joel.2.31">Joe 2:31</reference>). <div eID="gen25106" type="x-p"/>

Re 11:3 may refer to the same witnesses as at the transfiguration, Moses and Elijah; Re 11:6 identifies the latter (compare 1Ki 17:1 ; Jas 5:17 ). Even after the transfiguration Jesus ( Mt 17:11 ) speaks of Elijah's coming "to restore all things" as still future, though He adds that Elijah (in the person of John the Baptist) is come already in a sense (compare Ac 3:21 ). However, the future forerunner of Messiah at His second coming may be a prophet or number of prophets clothed with Elijah's power, who, with zealous upholders of "the law" clothed in the spirit of "Moses," may be the forerunning witnesses alluded to here and in Re 11:2-12 . The words "before the ... dreadful day of the Lord," show that John cannot be exclusively meant; for he came before the day of Christ's coming in grace, not before His coming in terror, of which last the destruction of Jerusalem was the earnest (Mal 4:1; Joe 2:31 ).
